subject: Marketplace bundling thresholds, invoice cadence, and distributor crediting
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@nebulahealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-06T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Bundle thresholds and distributor crediting question

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the throughput/latency profile. Procurement has a couple of questions before we finalize the private offer:

1) Our legal/finance team wants to understand how you treat bundled SKUs when we hit tier thresholds mid-quarter. For example, if we consume 2.2M tokens in month 2 of a 3-month billing period, does the bundle uplift apply retroactively to month 1?

2) We purchase through CloudDistributors in EMEA and they requested clarity on distributor credit routing. Currently they expect a passback credit on invoices at settlement rather than upfront reductions. Is that supported and what evidence will Redwood provide?

Attaching our committed volume spreadsheet for the first 12 months (nebula_commit_spreadsheet.xlsx).

Can we get a single page summary of how credits are applied and sample invoice line items so our finance team can sign off?

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Procurement Lead, Nebula Health
procurement@nebulahealth.com

---
Attachment: nebula_commit_spreadsheet.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, irene_choi@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-11-06T10:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Bundle thresholds and distributor crediting question

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions and the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (channel) and Irene (ops) to confirm routing and invoice examples. High-level answers below — I'll follow with a short PDF and sample invoice lines by end of day.

- Retroactive uplift: We support lookback adjustments at the billing period boundary (monthly/quarterly depending on the PO). If the committed tier is crossed during the period we can apply a retrospective credit for earlier usage in the same billing window; we do not automatically reprice prior closed invoices without an agreed true-up process.

- Distributor crediting: We can do either (a) passback at settlement as a credit note to the reseller, or (b) reduce the list price on Redwood's invoice and issue a separate credit statement to the distributor. Option (a) is the default for CloudDistributors-type partners. Documentation and sample lines coming.

Two asks from our side to make this concrete for finance:
1) Confirm preferred cadence (monthly true-up vs quarterly true-up).
2) Confirm who will receive Redwood's invoice (you vs CloudDistributors) and whether Nebula will process a reseller pass-through or prefer direct payment + distributor credit.

Irene and Ben — can you confirm the sample invoice lines and whether we need a special GL tag for distributor credits?

Thanks — attaching a concise matrix (redwood-bundle-pricing-matrix.pdf) that explains the uplift and credit types.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Date: 2026-11-06T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Bundle thresholds and distributor crediting question

Thanks Sam / Olga — quick channel perspective: we recommend monthly true-up for Nebula because it minimizes reconciliation friction for the distributor and allows earlier application of tiered discounts (helps Nebula's unit economics).

Sample invoice guidance (we'll produce CSV examples):
- Line 1000: Redwood Inference — Private Offer: Base compute tokens (list price)
- Line 1100: Discount applied (Private Offer discount ID 1234) — negative line reducing the base
- Line 1200: Distributor passback credit — issued as a credit memo referencing the reseller PO number (CloudDistributors PO # in memo)

For GL tagging: we can include a custom invoice code 'CD-REBATE' to make downstream ERP reconciliation simple. Irene, can ops add that field to the invoice export?

Ben Carter
Head of Channel Partnerships, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Bundle thresholds and distributor crediting question

Hi all — Marco from CloudDistributors here. Confirming we prefer settlement passback (credit note) at the end of each month. A couple operational notes for Nebula/Redwood to agree on:

- Credit memo reference: Please include the reseller invoice number and Nebula's PO reference. Our accounting requires the originating Redwood invoice + reseller PO for automated matching.
- Timing: We reconcile credits on day +15 after month close; please schedule credit memos within that window to avoid manual follow-up.
- Evidence: A CSV with monthly usage, tier applied, and credit calculation is required as supporting evidence.

We can accept the 'CD-REBATE' GL tag on the credit memo. Also, if Nebula wants earlier application of uplift to their internal reporting we can provide a monthly estimated memo, with final settlement as a credit.

Marco López
VP Sales — EMEA, CloudDistributors
